{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01TbKjBeueUP8NThChciMaEo","type":"tool_result","content":"// Package toml decodes TOML v1.0.0 documents using only the standard library.\npackage toml\n\nimport (\n\t\"errors\"\n\t\"fmt\"\n\t\"io\"\n\t\"strings\"\n\t\"unicode/utf8\"\n)\n\n// ErrSyntax reports a document that TOML v1.0.0 does not allow. Callers inspect\n// it with errors.Is; the wrapped message names the line that failed.\nvar ErrSyntax = errors.New(\"invalid TOML\")\n\n// Decode reads a TOML document from r and returns its tagged-value model.\n// Each leaf maps to {\"type\", \"value\"} with the value as a string; each table maps to\n// an object, and each array of tables maps to an array of objects.\n// Values are limited to strings, booleans, integers, and floats so far.\nfunc Decode(r io.Reader) (map[string]any, error) {\n\tdata, err := io.ReadAll(r)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, fmt.Errorf(\"read document: %w\", err)\n\t}\n\tif !utf8.Valid(data) {\n\t\treturn nil, fmt.Errorf(\"%w: document is not valid UTF-8\", ErrSyntax)\n\t}\n\tp := &parser{src: string(data)}\n\tdoc, err := p.document()\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, err\n\t}\n\treturn doc.export(), nil\n}\n\n// parser scans src by byte offset. Multi-byte runes are copied through unchanged,\n// so the ASCII delimiters the scanner checks are never confused with them.\ntype parser struct {\n\tsrc string\n\tpos int\n}\n\n// document reads every line into the root table. cur is the table that key/value pairs\n// land in; it changes at each header.\nfunc (p *parser) document() (*table, error) {\n\troot := newTable(originHeader)\n\tcur := root\n\tfor {\n\t\tp.skipSpaces()\n\t\tif p.done() {\n\t\t\treturn root, nil\n\t\t}\n\t\tswitch c := p.src[p.pos]; {\n\t\tcase c == '#' || c == '\\n' || c == '\\r':\n\t\t\tif err := p.endOfLine(); err != nil {\n\t\t\t\treturn nil, err\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\tcase c == '[':\n\t\t\tparts, array, err := p.header()\n\t\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\t\treturn nil, err\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tif cur, err = p.enterHeader(root, parts, array); err != nil {\n\t\t\t\treturn nil, err\n\t\t\t}\n\t\tdefault:\n\t\t\tparts, value, err := p.keyValue()\n\t\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\t\treturn nil, err\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tif err := p.insert(cur, parts, value); err != nil {\n\t\t\t\treturn nil, err\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t\tif err := p.endOfLine(); err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn nil, err\n\t\t}\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc (p *parser) keyValue() ([]string, any, error) {\n\tparts, err := p.key()\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, nil, err\n\t}\n\tname := strings.Join(parts, \".\")\n\tp.skipSpaces()\n\tif p.done() || p.src[p.pos] != '=' {\n\t\treturn nil, nil, p.errorf(\"expected '=' after key %q\", name)\n\t}\n\tp.pos++\n\tp.skipSpaces()\n\tvalue, err := p.value()\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, nil, err\n\t}\n\treturn parts, value, nil\n}\n\n// value reads one value. Strings start with a quote and arrays and inline tables with a\n// bracket or brace; everything else is a bare boolean, integer, or float. The result is\n// a tagged model, an arrayValue, or a closed *table. The longer string delimiters are\n// tested first so that `\"\"\"` is never read as `\"\"`.\nfunc (p *parser) value() (any, error) {\n\tif p.done() {\n\t\treturn nil, p.errorf(\"expected a value\")\n\t}\n\tvar s string\n\tvar err error\n\tswitch {\n\tcase strings.HasPrefix(p.src[p.pos:], `\"\"\"`):\n\t\ts, err = p.multiline('\"', true)\n\tcase p.src[p.pos] == '\"':\n\t\ts, err = p.basicString()\n\tcase strings.HasPrefix(p.src[p.pos:], \"'''\"):\n\t\ts, err = p.multiline('\\'', false)\n\tcase p.src[p.pos] == '\\'':\n\t\ts, err = p.literalString()\n\tcase p.src[p.pos] == '[':\n\t\treturn p.array()\n\tcase p.src[p.pos] == '{':\n\t\treturn p.inlineTable()\n\tdefault:\n\t\treturn p.scalar()\n\t}\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, err\n\t}\n\treturn map[string]any{\"type\": \"string\", \"value\": s}, nil\n}\n\n// endOfLine consumes trailing spaces, an optional comment, and the line break.\n// End of input also ends a line.\nfunc (p *parser) endOfLine() error {\n\tp.skipSpaces()\n\tif !p.done() && p.src[p.pos] == '#' {\n\t\tp.pos++\n\t\tfor !p.done() && !p.atNewline() {\n\t\t\tif isDisallowedControl(p.src[p.pos]) {\n\t\t\t\treturn p.errorf(\"control character in comment\")\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tp.pos++\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tif p.done() {\n\t\treturn nil\n\t}\n\tif p.src[p.pos] == '\\n' {\n\t\tp.pos++\n\t\treturn nil\n\t}\n\tif p.atCRLF() {\n\t\tp.pos += 2\n\t\treturn nil\n\t}\n\treturn p.errorf(\"unexpected text after value\")\n}\n\nfunc (p *parser) skipSpaces() {\n\tfor !p.done() && (p.src[p.pos] == ' ' || p.src[p.pos] == '\\t') {\n\t\tp.pos++\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc (p *parser) done() bool {\n\treturn p.pos >= len(p.src)\n}\n\nfunc (p *parser) atCRLF() bool {\n\treturn strings.HasPrefix(p.src[p.pos:], \"\\r\\n\")\n}\n\nfunc (p *parser) atNewline() bool {\n\treturn !p.done() && (p.src[p.pos] == '\\n' || p.atCRLF())\n}\n\nfunc (p *parser) errorf(format string, args ...any) error {\n\tline := 1 + strings.Count(p.src[:p.pos], \"\\n\")\n\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"%w: line %d: %s\", ErrSyntax, line, fmt.Sprintf(format, args...))\n}\n\nfunc isBareKeyByte(c byte) bool {\n\treturn (c >= 'A' && c <= 'Z') || (c >= 'a' && c <= 'z') || (c >= '0' && c <= '9') || c == '-' || c == '_'\n}\n\n// isDisallowedControl reports whether c is a control character TOML forbids in\n// strings and comments. Tab is the only control character it allows. Line breaks\n// are excluded here because each caller decides whether a line break is legal.\nfunc isDisallowedControl(c byte) bool {\n\treturn (c < 0x20 && c != '\\t' && c != '\\n') || c == 0x7f\n}\npackage toml\n\nimport (\n\t\"fmt\"\n\t\"math\"\n\t\"regexp\"\n\t\"strconv\"\n\t\"strings\"\n)\n\n// Each pattern is the TOML v1.0.0 grammar for one form. Underscores sit only between\n// digits, and leading zeros are allowed only in the fraction and exponent of a float.\nvar (\n\tdecimalIntPattern   = regexp.MustCompile(`^[+-]?(0|[1-9](_?[0-9])*)$`)\n\thexIntPattern       = regexp.MustCompile(`^0x[0-9A-Fa-f](_?[0-9A-Fa-f])*$`)\n\toctalIntPattern     = regexp.MustCompile(`^0o[0-7](_?[0-7])*$`)\n\tbinaryIntPattern    = regexp.MustCompile(`^0b[01](_?[01])*$`)\n\tfloatPattern        = regexp.MustCompile(`^[+-]?(0|[1-9](_?[0-9])*)((\\.[0-9](_?[0-9])*)([eE][+-]?[0-9](_?[0-9])*)?|[eE][+-]?[0-9](_?[0-9])*)$`)\n\tspecialFloatPattern = regexp.MustCompile(`^[+-]?(inf|nan)$`)\n)\n\n// scalar reads the bare token at p.pos and classifies it as a boolean, integer, or float.\n// The whole token must match one grammar, so a partly valid token is rejected, not truncated.\nfunc (p *parser) scalar() (map[string]any, error) {\n\tstart := p.pos\n\tfor !p.done() && isScalarByte(p.src[p.pos]) {\n\t\tp.pos++\n\t}\n\ttoken := p.src[start:p.pos]\n\tswitch {\n\tcase token == \"\":\n\t\treturn nil, p.errorf(\"expected a value\")\n\tcase token == \"true\" || token == \"false\":\n\t\treturn tagged(\"bool\", token), nil\n\tcase specialFloatPattern.MatchString(token):\n\t\treturn tagged(\"float\", formatFloat(parseSpecialFloat(token))), nil\n\tcase isInteger(token):\n\t\tn, err := parseInteger(token)\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn nil, p.errorf(\"%v\", err)\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn tagged(\"integer\", strconv.FormatInt(n, 10)), nil\n\tcase floatPattern.MatchString(token):\n\t\tf, err := strconv.ParseFloat(stripUnderscores(token), 64)\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn nil, p.errorf(\"float %s is outside the binary64 range\", token)\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn tagged(\"float\", formatFloat(f)), nil\n\t}\n\treturn nil, p.errorf(\"invalid value %q\", token)\n}\n\n// isScalarByte reports whether c can appear in a bare boolean, integer, or float token.\nfunc isScalarByte(c byte) bool {\n\treturn (c >= 'A' && c <= 'Z') || (c >= 'a' && c <= 'z') || (c >= '0' && c <= '9') ||\n\t\tc == '+' || c == '-' || c == '_' || c == '.'\n}\n\nfunc isInteger(token string) bool {\n\treturn decimalIntPattern.MatchString(token) || hexIntPattern.MatchString(token) ||\n\t\toctalIntPattern.MatchString(token) || binaryIntPattern.MatchString(token)\n}\n\n// parseInteger converts a token that {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_018vA69aBH6R11LfxAR3V6Te","type":"tool_result","content":"package toml\n\nimport (\n\t\"strings\"\n)\n\n// maxScalar is the largest Unicode code point, U+10FFFF.\nconst maxScalar = 0x10FFFF\n\n// simpleEscapes are the one-character escapes TOML v1.0.0 lists for basic strings.\nvar simpleEscapes = map[byte]string{\n\t'b':  \"\\b\",\n\t't':  \"\\t\",\n\t'n':  \"\\n\",\n\t'f':  \"\\f\",\n\t'r':  \"\\r\",\n\t'\"':  \"\\\"\",\n\t'\\\\': \"\\\\\",\n}\n\n// basicString reads a single-line basic string at p.pos, which holds the opening quote.\nfunc (p *parser) basicString() (string, error) {\n\tp.pos++\n\tvar b strings.Builder\n\tfor {\n\t\tif p.done() || p.atNewline() {\n\t\t\treturn \"\", p.errorf(\"unterminated basic string\")\n\t\t}\n\t\tc := p.src[p.pos]\n\t\tswitch {\n\t\tcase c == '\"':\n\t\t\tp.pos++\n\t\t\treturn b.String(), nil\n\t\tcase c == '\\\\':\n\t\t\ts, err := p.escape()\n\t\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\t\treturn \"\", err\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tb.WriteString(s)\n\t\tcase isDisallowedControl(c):\n\t\t\treturn \"\", p.errorf(\"control character in basic string\")\n\t\tdefault:\n\t\t\tb.WriteByte(c)\n\t\t\tp.pos++\n\t\t}\n\t}\n}\n\n// literalString reads a single-line literal string at p.pos, which holds the opening\n// quote. Nothing inside is escaped.\nfunc (p *parser) literalString() (string, error) {\n\tp.pos++\n\tstart := p.pos\n\tfor !p.done() && p.src[p.pos] != '\\'' {\n\t\tif p.atNewline() || isDisallowedControl(p.src[p.pos]) {\n\t\t\treturn \"\", p.errorf(\"invalid character in literal string\")\n\t\t}\n\t\tp.pos++\n\t}\n\tif p.done() {\n\t\treturn \"\", p.errorf(\"unterminated literal string\")\n\t}\n\ts := p.src[start:p.pos]\n\tp.pos++\n\treturn s, nil\n}\n\n// multiline reads a multi-line string whose delimiter is quote repeated three times.\n// Escapes apply only when escapes is true, which is the basic form. A line break right\n// after the opening delimiter is trimmed. Up to two extra quotes may sit directly before\n// the closing delimiter.\nfunc (p *parser) multiline(quote byte, escapes bool) (string, error) {\n\tp.pos += 3\n\tp.trimOpeningNewline()\n\tvar b strings.Builder\n\tfor {\n\t\tif p.done() {\n\t\t\treturn \"\", p.errorf(\"unterminated multi-line string\")\n\t\t}\n\t\tc := p.src[p.pos]\npackage toml\n\n// origin records how a table came to exist. A later [header] or dotted key consults\n// it to decide whether it may add to or define the table.\ntype origin int\n\nconst (\n\t// originImplicit marks a super-table created only as a step on a longer header\n\t// path, such as a for [a.b]. A later [a] header may still define it.\n\toriginImplicit origin = iota\n\t// originHeader marks a table defined by its own [name] header, or an element\n\t// created by a [[name]] header. No later header may define it again.\n\toriginHeader\n\t// originDotted marks a table created by a dotted key. Later dotted keys may extend\n\t// it, but no header may define it.\n\toriginDotted\n\t// originInline marks an inline table. It is closed: neither a dotted key nor a\n\t// header may add a key to it once its braces have closed.\n\toriginInline\n)\n\n// table holds the entries of one TOML table while a document is read. Each entry is a\n// *table, a tableArray, or the tagged map that a value returns. The three dynamic types\n// differ, so a table is never mistaken for a value.\ntype table struct {\n\tentries map[string]any\n\torigin  origin\n}\n\n// tableArray is the value of a [[name]] key. Each element is one table, defined by one\n// header, in document order.\ntype tableArray []*table\n\nfunc newTable(o origin) *table {\n\treturn &table{entries: map[string]any{}, origin: o}\n}\n\n// header reads a [name] or [[name]] line through its closing brackets. It returns the\n// key parts and whether the header is an array header. Underscores sit only between\n// digits, and leading zeros are allowed only in the fraction and exponent of a float.\nvar (\n\tdecimalIntPattern   = regexp.MustCompile(`^[+-]?(0|[1-9](_?[0-9])*)$`)\n\thexIntPattern       = regexp.MustCompile(`^0x[0-9A-Fa-f](_?[0-9A-Fa-f])*$`)\n\toctalIntPattern     = regexp.MustCompile(`^0o[0-7](_?[0-7])*$`)\n\tbinaryIntPattern    = regexp.MustCompile(`^0b[01](_?[01])*$`)\n\tfloatPattern        = regexp.MustCompile(`^[+-]?(0|[1-9](_?[0-9])*)((\\.[0-9](_?[0-9])*)([eE][+-]?[0-9](_?[0-9])*)?|[eE][+-]?[0-9](_?[0-9])*)$`)\n\tspecialFloatPattern = regexp.MustCompile(`^[+-]?(inf|nan)$`)\n)\n\n// scalar reads the bare token at p.pos and classifies it as a boolean, integer, or float.\n// The whole token must match one grammar, so a partly valid token is rejected, not truncated.\nfunc (p *parser) scalar() (map[string]any, error) {\n\tstart := p.pos\n\tfor !p.done() && isScalarByte(p.src[p.pos]) {\n\t\tp.pos++\n\t}\n\ttoken := p.src[start:p.pos]\n\tswitch {\n\tcase token == \"\":\n\t\treturn nil, p.errorf(\"expected a value\")\n\tcase token == \"true\" || token == \"false\":\n\t\treturn tagged(\"bool\", token), nil\n\tcase specialFloatPattern.MatchString(token):\n\t\treturn tagged(\"float\", formatFloat(parseSpecialFloat(token))), nil\n\tcase isInteger(token):\n\t\tn, err := parseInteger(token)\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn nil, p.errorf(\"%v\", err)\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn tagged(\"integer\", strconv.FormatInt(n, 10)), nil\n\tcase floatPattern.MatchString(token):\n\t\tf, err := strconv.ParseFloat(stripUnderscores(token), 64)\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn nil, p.errorf(\"float %s is outside the binary64 range\", token)\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn tagged(\"float\", formatFloat(f)), nil\n\t}\n\treturn nil, p.errorf(\"invalid value %q\", token)\n}\n\n// isScalarByte reports whether c can appear in a bare boolean, integer, or float token.\nfunc isScalarByte(c byte) bool {\n\treturn (c >= 'A' && c <= 'Z') || (c >= 'a' && c <= 'z') || (c >= '0' && c <= '9') ||\n\t\tc == '+' || c == '-' || c == '_' || c == '.'\n}\n\nfunc isInteger(token string) bool {\n\treturn decimalIntPattern.MatchString(token) || hexIntPattern.MatchString(token) ||\n\t\toctalIntPattern.MatchString(token) || binaryIntPattern.MatchString(token)\n}\n\n// parseInteger converts a token that passed isInteger to a signed 64-bit value. A value\n// outside that range is an error, never a rounded or wrapped result.\nfunc parseInteger(token string) (int64, error) {\n\tdigits := stripUnderscores(token)\n\tbase := 10\n\tswitch {\n\tcase hexIntPattern.MatchString(token):\n\t\tbase, digits = 16, digits[2:]\n\tcase octalIntPattern.MatchString(token):\n\t\tbase, digits = 8, digits[2:]\n\tcase binaryIntPattern.MatchString(token):\n\t\tbase, digits = 2, digits[2:]\n\t}\n\tn, err := strconv.ParseInt(digits, base, 64)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn 0, fmt.Errorf(\"integer %s is outside the signed 64-bit range\", token)\n\t}\n\treturn n, nil\n}\n\n// parseSpecialFloat maps a token that passed specialFloatPattern to its IEEE 754 value.\nfunc parseSpecialFloat(token string) float64 {\n\tswitch {\n\tcase strings.HasSuffix(token, \"nan\"):\n\t\treturn math.NaN()\n\tcase strings.HasPrefix(token, \"-\"):\n\t\treturn math.Inf(-1)\n\t}\n\treturn math.Inf(1)\n}\n\n// formatFloat renders a float as the shortest decimal that reads back to the same\n// binary64 value. Special values use the TOML spelling without a leading plus.\nfunc formatFloat(f float64) string {\n\tswitch {\n\tcase math.IsNaN(f):\n\t\treturn \"nan\"\n\tcase math.IsInf(f, 1):\n\t\treturn \"inf\"\n\tcase math.IsInf(f, -1):\n\t\treturn \"-inf\"\n\t}\n\treturn strconv.FormatFloat(f, 'g', -1, 64)\n}\n\nfunc stripUnderscores(token string) string {\n\treturn strings.ReplaceAll(token, \"_\", \"\")\n}\n\n// tagged builds the {\"type\", \"value\"} model for a scalar whose value is already a string.\nfunc tagged(kind, value string) map[string]any {\n\treturn map[string]any{\"type\": kind, \"value\": value}\n}\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":22,"oldLines":6,"newStart":22,"newLines":9,"lines":[" // scalar reads the bare token at p.pos and classifies it as a boolean, integer, or float."," // The whole token must match one grammar, so a partly valid token is rejected, not truncated."," func (p *parser) scalar() (map[string]any, error) {","+  if tv, ok, err := p.temporal(); ok {","+    return tv, err","+  }","   start := p.pos","   for !p.done() && isScalarByte(p.src[p.pos]) {","     p.pos++"]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false,"contentNotInModelContext":true},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_01BGq2WgJAYfB4uB27sV99Bt","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

Underscores sit only between\n// digits, and leading zeros are allowed only in the fraction and exponent of a float.\nvar (\n\tdecimalIntPattern   = regexp.MustCompile(`^[+-]?(0|[1-9](_?[0-9])*)$`)\n\thexIntPattern       = regexp.MustCompile(`^0x[0-9A-Fa-f](_?[0-9A-Fa-f])*$`)\n\toctalIntPattern     = regexp.MustCompile(`^0o[0-7](_?[0-7])*$`)\n\tbinaryIntPattern    = regexp.MustCompile(`^0b[01](_?[01])*$`)\n\tfloatPattern        = regexp.MustCompile(`^[+-]?(0|[1-9](_?[0-9])*)((\\.[0-9](_?[0-9])*)([eE][+-]?[0-9](_?[0-9])*)?|[eE][+-]?[0-9](_?[0-9])*)$`)\n\tspecialFloatPattern = regexp.MustCompile(`^[+-]?(inf|nan)$`)\n)\n\n// scalar reads the bare token at p.pos and classifies it as a boolean, integer, or float.\n// The whole token must match one grammar, so a partly valid token is rejected, not truncated.\nfunc (p *parser) scalar() (map[string]any, error) {\n\tif tv, ok, err := p.temporal(); Callers inspect\n// it with errors.Is; the wrapped message names the line that failed.\nvar ErrSyntax = errors.New(\"invalid TOML\")\n\n// Decode reads a TOML document from r and returns its tagged-value model.\n// Each leaf maps to {\"type\", \"value\"} with the value as a string; each table maps to\n// an object, and each array of tables maps to an array of objects.\n// Values are limited to strings, booleans, integers, and floats so far.\nfunc Decode(r io.Reader) (map[string]any, error) {\n\tdata, err := io.ReadAll(r)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, fmt.Errorf(\"read document: %w\", err)\n\t}\n\tif !utf8.Valid(data) {\n\t\treturn nil, fmt.Errorf(\"%w: document is not valid UTF-8\", ErrSyntax)\n\t}\n\tp := &parser{src: string(data)}\n\tdoc, err := p.document()\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, err\n\t}\n\treturn doc.export(), nil\n}\n\n// parser scans src by byte offset. Multi-byte runes are copied through unchanged,\n// so the ASCII delimiters the scanner checks are never confused with them.\ntype parser struct {\n\tsrc string\n\tpos int\n}\n\n// document reads every line into the root table. cur is the table that key/value pairs\n// land in; it changes at each header.\nfunc (p *parser) document() (*table, error) {\n\troot := newTable(originHeader)\n\tcur := root\n\tfor {\n\t\tp.skipSpaces()\n\t\tif p.done() {\n\t\t\treturn root, nil\n\t\t}\n\t\tswitch c := p.src[p.pos]; {\n\t\tcase c == '#' || c == '\\n' || c == '\\r':\n\t\t\tif err := p.endOfLine(); err != nil {\n\t\t\t\treturn nil, err\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\tcase c == '[':\n\t\t\tparts, array, err := p.header()\n\t\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\t\treturn nil, err\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tif cur, err = p.enterHeader(root, parts, array); err != nil {\n\t\t\t\treturn nil, err\n\t\t\t}\n\t\tdefault:\n\t\t\tparts, value, err := p.keyValue()\n\t\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\t\treturn nil, err\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tif err := p.insert(cur, parts, value); err != nil {\n\t\t\t\treturn nil, err\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t\tif err := p.endOfLine(); err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn nil, err\n\t\t}\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc (p *parser) keyValue() ([]string, any, error) {\n\tparts, err := p.key()\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, nil, err\n\t}\n\tname := strings.Join(parts, \".\")\n\tp.skipSpaces()\n\tif p.done() || p.src[p.pos] != '=' {\n\t\treturn nil, nil, p.errorf(\"expected '=' after key %q\", name)\n\t}\n\tp.pos++\n\tp.skipSpaces()\n\tvalue, err := p.value()\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, nil, err\n\t}\n\treturn parts, value, nil\n}\n\n// value reads one value. Strings start with a quote and arrays and inline tables with a\n// bracket or brace; everything else is a bare boolean, integer, or float. The result is\n// a tagged model, an arrayValue, or a closed *table. The longer string delimiters are\n// tested first so that `\"\"\"` is never read as `\"\"`.\nfunc (p *parser) value() (any, error) {\n\tif p.done() {\n\t\treturn nil, p.errorf(\"expected a value\")\n\t}\n\tvar s string\n\tvar err error\n\tswitch {\n\tcase strings.HasPrefix(p.src[p.pos:], `\"\"\"`):\n\t\ts, err = p.multiline('\"', true)\n\tcase p.src[p.pos] == '\"':\n\t\ts, err = {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01F4qP7TPyyoMWE9VSGQEfmo","type":"tool_result","content":"The \"test\" command runs the test cases.\n\nThe way toml-test works is that for every test case it executes a \"decoder\"\ncommand, which reads TOML from stdin and then outputs JSON describing that TOML\n(or returns an error if it thinks the TOML isn't valid). Encoder tests work the\nsame except in reverse: it reads JSON and transforms that to TOML.\n\nThere are three types of tests:\n\n    valid      Valid TOML that the decoder command should describe as JSON.\n    invalid    Invalid TOML files that should be rejected with an error.\n    encoder    JSON that the encoder command should transform to TOML.\n\n\u001b[1mImplementing a decoder:\u001b[0m\n\n    A decoder reads TOML data from stdin and outputs a JSON description to\n    stdout and exits with code 0. If the TOML data is invalid, it must exit\n    with code 1. It's recommended to write an error message to stderr.\n\n    An example in pseudocode:\n\n        toml_data = read_stdin()\n\n        parsed_toml = decode_toml(toml_data)\n\n        if error_parsing_toml():\n            print_error_to_stderr()\n            exit(1)\n\n        print_as_json_description(parsed_toml)\n        exit(0)\n\n    Details of the JSON format is explained below in \"JSON description\".\n\n\u001b[1mImplementing an encoder:\u001b[0m\n\n    An encoder is the reverse of a decoder; it reads a JSON description from\n    stdin converts that to TOML.\n\n    An example in pseudocode:\n\n        json_data = read_stdin()\n\n        json_description = decode_json(json_data)\n\n        print_as_toml(json_description)\n        exit(0)\n\n\u001b[1mJSON description\u001b[0m\n\n    TOML is described with JSON as follows:\n\n    - TOML tables correspond to JSON objects.\n    - TOML arrays correspond to JSON arrays.\n    - TOML values correspond to a JSON object of the form:\n      {\"type\": \"{TOML_TYPE}\", \"value\": \"{TOML_VALUE}\"}\n\n    In the above, TOML_VALUE is always a JSON string (even for integers or\n    bools), and TOML_TYPE may be one of: string, integer, float, bool,\n    datetime, datetime-local, date-local, or time-local.\ninvalid/array/double-comma-01.toml\ninvalid/array/double-comma-02.toml\ninvalid/array/extend-defined-aot.toml\ninvalid/array/extending-table.toml\ninvalid/array/missing-separator-01.toml\nShell cwd was reset to /mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/Toml/runs/20261014.124728/build/toml","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"a8f64c0b-dc50-478d-940e-5a49a22f3f38","uuid":"39beb348-a0b3-47f5-98fe-7ebf11c071ab","timestamp":"2026-10-14T13:34:25.551Z","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"The \"test\" command runs the test cases.\n\nThe way toml-test works is that for every test case it executes a \"decoder\"\ncommand, which reads TOML from stdin and then outputs JSON describing that TOML\n(or returns an error if it thinks the TOML isn't valid). Encoder tests work the\nsame except in reverse: it reads JSON and transforms that to TOML.\n\nThere are three types of tests:\n\n    valid      Valid TOML that the decoder command should describe as JSON.\n    invalid    Invalid TOML files that should be rejected with an error.\n    encoder    JSON that the encoder command should transform to TOML.\n\n\u001b[1mImplementing a decoder:\u001b[0m\n\n    A decoder reads TOML data from stdin and outputs a JSON description to\n    stdout and exits with code 0. If the TOML data is invalid, it must exit\n    with code 1. It's recommended to write an error message to stderr.\n\n    An example in pseudocode:\n\n        toml_data = read_stdin()\n\n        parsed_toml = decode_toml(toml_data)\n\n        if error_parsing_toml():\n            print_error_to_stderr()\n            exit(1)\n\n        print_as_json_description(parsed_toml)\n        exit(0)\n\n    Details of the JSON format is explained below in \"JSON description\".\n\n\u001b[1mImplementing an encoder:\u001b[0m\n\n    An encoder is the reverse of a decoder; it reads a JSON description from\n    stdin converts that to TOML.\n\n    An example in pseudocode:\n\n        json_data = read_stdin()\n\n        json_description = decode_json(json_data)\n\n        print_as_toml(json_description)\n        exit(0)\n\n\u001b[1mJSON description\u001b[0m\n\n    TOML is described with JSON as follows:\n\n    - TOML tables correspond to JSON objects.\n    - TOML arrays correspond to JSON arrays.\n    - TOML values correspond to a JSON object of the form:\n      {\"type\": \"{TOML_TYPE}\", \"value\": \"{TOML_VALUE}\"}\n\n    In the above, TOML_VALUE is always a JSON string (even for integers or\n    bools), and TOML_TYPE may be one of: string, integer, float, bool,\n    datetime, datetime-local, date-local, or time-local.\ninvalid/array/double-comma-01.toml\ninvalid/array/double-comma-02.toml\ninvalid/array/extend-defined-aot.toml\ninvalid/array/extending-table.toml\ninvalid/array/missing-separator-01.toml","stderr":"\nShell cwd was reset to /mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/Toml/runs/20261014.124728/build/toml","interrupted":false,"isImage":false,"noOutputExpected":false},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_01F4qP7TPyyoMWE9VSGQEfmo","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01UdKM9sAhQDXJBF6ia9P8BX","type":"tool_result","content":"50:    -script        Print a small bash/zsh script with -skip flag for failing\n51-                   tests; useful to get a list of \"known failures\" for CI\n52-                   integrations and such.\n53-\n54:    -toml          TOML version to run tests for, 1.0 or 1.1. Default is 1.0.\n55-\n56:    -timeout       Maximum time for a single test run, to detect infinite loops\n57-                   or pathological cases.
